title: [RFC]: Support Prefill Context Parallel (PCP)
body: ### Motivation. A follow-up to add prefill context parallel(PCP) after DCP (PR [#23734](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23734)) to optimize TTFT. In DCP, the KV Cache is partitioned along the sequence dimension into several segments (interleave style), achieving context parallelism during the decode phase. --- --- --- Similarly, PCP will split the entire request along the sequence dimension during the prefill phase and further partitions the KVCache along the sequence dimension. ### Proposed Change. Aside from the attention module, almost all other modules do not involve contextual dependencies and can naturally adapt to context parallelism. In the attention module, we adopt the following strategy to implement PCP (chunked prefill is not considered for now), marked as **red.** First, for the KV, we perform an AllGather op along the sequence dimension within the PCP group to obtain the complete KV values. Then, the kvcache is stored according to the slot_mapping. For attention computation, since we have obtained the complete KV, we only need to carefully design the custom mask and perform normal attention. During the decode phase, modules other than attention involve redundant computations (since num new tokens = 1) across PCP group. In the attention module, we first execute the original DCP computation logic within the respective PCP group. Then, before updating the attention output using lse, we perform an AllGather within the PCP group to obtain complete sequence information. And the subsequent steps remain unaffected. **Summary** - **The creation of Prefill Context Parallel communication domains.** Unlike DCP communication domains, which are subdivisions within the TP domain, PCP communication domains stand alongside DP, PP, and TP, and affect the total device count allocation. - **Modification of slot_mapping calculation.​​** Building upon the ​​virtual block​​ concept introduced by DCP, PCP will continue to utilize virtual blocks within each PCP group. Each PCP group will be responsible for storing the portion of the KV Cache that corresponds to its assigned segment of the sequence. - **Modification of parameter calculations in the ModelRunner.​​** The calculation of parameters such as sequence length and token count must be updated, as these values are now influenced and scaled by the ​​PCP size​​. - **Modification of the attention backend computation logic.** The core attention calculation requires changes to handle the distributed KV Cache across PCP groups. The specific algorithmic updates are detailed in the red markings within the provided schematic diagram. ### Feedback Period. We will complete the above modifications and submit a PR within 1-2 weeks ### Co-Authors @zhenwenqi2024 @FENP ### CC List. @youkaichao @njhill @WoosukKwon @ruisearch42 @youzhedian ### Any Other Things. Here are some related issues and PRs: DCP: PR [#23734](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23734), PR [#24864](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24864), PR [#25438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25438) PCP: RFC [#22693](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22693), RFC [#7519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/7519) ### Roadmap - [x] Basic feature #28718 - [ ] PCP support for GQA #49564 - [x] PCP support for PIECEWISE CUDAGraph; #53869 #53515 - [x] PCP support for MLA #50034; Feature works (These items will be tackled in follow-up PRs; community contributions are warmly welcomed.): - [ ] PCP support other backends; - [ ] PCP support for SpecDecoding: MTP&DSpark #53427 - [ ] PCP support for P/D disaggregation; - [ ] PCP support for CUDAFullGraph; #53867 - [ ] Ring-CP style attention backend algorithm, ref RFC #26133.

title: [RFC]: Prefill Context Parallel for Qwen3.5 Hybrid Attention
body: ## Summary This RFC describes the implementation of Prefill Context Parallel (PCP) for Qwen3.5's hybrid attention architecture, which combines full attention and linear attention (GatedDeltaNet) layers. PCP reduces long-context prefill latency by: - **Full attention layers**: Distributing sequence tokens across ranks using zigzag ring attention (cp_size speedup per layer) - **Linear attention**: Splitting batch dimension instead of sequence, eliminating replicated computation and all_gather overhead - **MoE layers**: Spliting tokens dimension ## Motivation Long-context prefill is a major bottleneck for LLM inference: 1. **Quadratic attention complexity**: Full attention is O(N^2) in sequence length, making 256K+ contexts extremely slow 2. **Memory bandwidth** : Large KV caches stress memory subsystem Tensor Parallelism (TP) helps by distributing model weights, but each GPU still processes the full sequence. Context Parallel (CP) addresses this by distributing the sequence itself across GPUs. ### Challenge: Hybrid Attention Qwen3.5 uses a hybrid architecture: - **15 full attention layers**: Standard transformer attention - **45 linear attention layers**: GatedDeltaNet (GDN) with recurrent state Linear attention has a key constraint: the recurrent state at position is depends on ALL previous tokens. This means naive token splitting breaks correctness for linear attention layers. ## Design ### Architecture Overview The complete picture showing data distribution and communication across all layer types: ### Token Distribution PCP uses **zigzag distribution** to balance tokens across ranks: ``` Input sequence: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, ...] With cp_size = C: Rank 0: [0, C, C+1, 2C, 2C+1, ...] (positions where pos % C in {0, C-1, ...}) Rank 1: [1, C-1, C+2, 2C-1, ...] (positions where pos % C in {1, C-2, ...}) ... Rank r: [r, ...] (positions where pos % C == r or similar pattern) ``` This interleaving ensures each rank has tokens from all parts of the sequence, improving load balance for causal attention. For cp_size = 2 specifically: ``` Rank 0: [0, 3, 4, 7, 8, ...] (positions 0, 3, 4, 7, ...) Rank 1: [1, 2, 5, 6, 9, ...] (positions 1, 2, 5, 6, ...) ``` ### Layer-Type Handling #### Full Attention Layers (Ring Attention) Full attention layers use **zigzag ring attention**: ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Ring Attention (Full Attn) │ │ │ │ Rank r Rank (r+1) mod C │ │ ┌────────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │ │ │ Q (local) │ │ Q (local) │ │ │ │ K (local) │ ─────────── P2P send ───────► │ K (recv) │ │ │ │ V (local) │ ─────────── P2P send ────────► │ V (recv) │ │ │ └────────────┘ └────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ │ │ Attention(Q_local, K_all, V_all) Attention(Q_local, ...) │ │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────── LSE merge ──────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ where C = cp_size (number of PCP ranks) ``` Each rank: 1. Computes local Q @ local K/V 2. Sends K/V to next rank via P2P 3. Receives K/V from previous rank 4. Accumulates attention outputs with LSE merge 5. Repeats for `cp_size` rounds **Benefit**: Each rank has N/cp_size query tokens, but still attends to all N keys via ring exchange. Computation per rank: (N/cp_size) × N = N²/cp_size → **cp_size speedup** (not cp_size², because each Q still needs all K/V for causal). #### Linear Attention Layers (Batch Split) Linear attention requires the full sequence per item due to recurrent state dependency. We split by **batch dimension** instead of sequence - Linear attention has no cross-item dependency: each item's recurrent state only depends on that item's history - Each rank has B/C items, each with FULL sequence S **Key insight**: Split by batch, not sequence. This gives each rank the full sequence it needs without any all_gather communication. ## Work Plan Each item below is scoped for a separate pull request. | PR | Item | Description | |----|------|-------------| | 1 | **Ring attention on full-attention layers** | Integrate `zigzag_ring_prefill_kv` into full-attention layers; handle zigzag token distribution, P2P K/V exchange, and LSE merge (`flash_attn.py`, `ring.py`) | | 2 | **Reshuffle calls** | Implement all-to-all activation reshuffle between seq-split and batch-split at layer group boundaries | | 3 | **Decode path** | Implement per-step LSE-weighted merge across PCP ranks for full-attn layers during decode (`flash_attn.py`) | | 4 | **Chunked Prefill** | Support chunked prefill with PCP, including handling cached KV attention and ring attention for current chunk | | 5 | **Support prefix cache** | Enable prefix cache when PCP is enabled | cc @lowintelligence @Orion34-lanbo

title: [RFC]: Unify Context Parallelism in vLLM (PCP ⊥ DCP)
body:
### Motivation.

Long-context serving needs to scale a *single* request across GPUs along two independent axes:

- **Prefill** is compute/comm-bound on the long prompt. **Prefill Context Parallel (PCP)** splits the prefill *sequence* across ranks (zigzag attention + LSE merge), cutting prefill latency.
- **Decode** is memory-bound on the growing KV cache. **Decode Context Parallel (DCP)** *shards* each KV head's cache across ranks, cutting decode KV memory.

These two axes are **orthogonal**: which rank owns a given decode KV shard has nothing to do with how the prefill sequence was split. A 1M-context request realistically wants **both** — prefill split across `pcp` ranks *and* decode KV split across `dcp` ranks — so the combined `pcp > 1, dcp > 1` case must work, cleanly and without redundancy.

**Today, vLLM cannot do that:**

- **DCP is shipped** GQA and MLA works — but only for `pcp = 1`.
- **PCP is not shipped.** Main Branch has PCP infrastructure (the `--pcp` flag, PCP process groups, the `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` config) but no PCP runtime (`PCPManager`). There are attempts for dsv4 like #43809, and the GQA attempt on FlashAttention in #46330 try to introduce `PCPManager` and `forward_with_pcp` in FA, but only for `dcp = 1`
- More fundamentally, the shipped CP infrastructure already bakes in a multiplicative model: `total_cp_world_size = pcp_world_size × dcp_world_size`, with DCP nested inside the TP group. This was designed assuming PCP and DCP are two factors of one CP group.  #28988's own limitation note says it plainly: *"every PCP rank holds the full set of decode tokens, leading to significant redundant communication and computation… we recommend enabling PCP on P instances in a P/D-disaggregation case."*


### Proposed Change.

Adopt the **orthogonal-groups** design from #33403 (Lucas Wilkinson): three independent rank axes instead of one multiplicative CP.

- **TP** shards heads.
- **PCP** shards the **prefill sequence** (compute only).
- **DCP** shards the **decode KV cache**.
- **KV shard count = `dcp_size`** — *not* `pcp × dcp`.

### First-pass scope: two clean DCP configurations

Rather than support arbitrary `(tp, pcp, dcp)` from day one, the first implementation should restrict DCP to two configurations where the decode communication pattern is clean. Both reuse the TP=2, PCP=2 base layout above.

**Case 1 — `DCP = PCP` (e.g. PCP=2, TP=2, DCP=2).** The DCP group *is* the PCP group, and its members share the same TP position, so they already hold the same Q heads. KV head `k0`'s cache is split into `s0` (rank 0) and `s1` (rank 2):

```
          tp0                    tp1
       +-------------------+-------------------+
pcp0   | 0: q0-3/k0/s0/p0  | 1: q4-7/k1/s0/p0  |
       +-------------------+-------------------+
pcp1   | 2: q0-3/k0/s1/p1  | 3: q4-7/k1/s1/p1  |
       +-------------------+-------------------+
DCP0 (k0): [0,2]   DCP1 (k1): [1,3]
```

Per decode layer, each rank computes attention of its Q against its local KV shard → partial output + LSE, then:

- **No Q all-gather** — Q heads are identical within the DCP group (same TP position).
- **All-reduce across the DCP group** (LSE-weighted combine of the KV shards) → each rank has the full attention output for its heads.
- **No scatter** — each rank keeps its original heads; `o_proj` proceeds per-TP-rank as usual.

This is the minimal pattern: replicated Q, sharded KV, all-reduce output.

**Case 2 — `DCP = TP × PCP` (e.g. PCP=2, TP=2, DCP=4).** The DCP group spans the entire TP×PCP block. Each rank holds one shard of one KV head; every KV head's full cache is reconstructed across the group:

```
          tp0                    tp1
       +-------------------+-------------------+
pcp0   | 0: q0-3/k0/s0/p0  | 1: q4-7/k1/s2/p0  |
       +-------------------+-------------------+
pcp1   | 2: q0-3/k0/s1/p1  | 3: q4-7/k1/s3/p1  |
       +-------------------+-------------------+
DCP0: [0,2,1,3]   (all ranks)
```

Per decode layer:

- **Full TP all-gather of Q** → every rank gets all H query heads.
- Each rank computes attention of *all* Q against its local KV shard → partial output [all H heads] + LSE.
- **Reduce-scatter across the DCP group `[0,2,1,3]`**: all-reduce to combine the KV shards, then scatter so each rank receives only its TP-local Q heads' output. Optimization: **all-reduce across the PCP pair `{0,2}`/`{1,3}` + reduce-scatter across TP `{0,1}`/`{2,3}`**, which moves fewer bytes than one flat reduce-scatter over all four.

This is the maximal pattern: gathered Q, sharded KV, reduce-scatter output.

These two cover the replicated-Q (`dcp = pcp`) and gathered-Q (`dcp = tp × pcp`) ends of the design space. Irregular middle cases — where the DCP group neither coincides with PCP nor exhausts the TP×PCP block — are deferred, since they require partial/irregular head gathering with no comm savings over Case 2.

### Feedback Period.

- **Phase 0 — Correctness baseline (#46330).** GQA PCP on FlashAttention, `dcp == 1`. First working GQA PCP, scoped to `dcp == 1` and non-hybrid attention, while delivering PCP fundamental runtime
- **Phase 1 — Unify PCP ⊥ DCP (core topology PR).** Move from multiplicative/nested to orthogonal: DCP groups span PCP and are orthogonal to TP; `total_cp_world_size` → `dcp_world_size`; decode no longer replicated across PCP (reuse the MLA DCP `a2a` partial-output + LSE-merge path); slot kernel places by DCP-shard ownership only. Add correctness gates for `pcp=2,dcp=2` and `pcp=2,dcp=4`. **First pass restricts DCP to the two clean cases above** (`dcp = pcp` and `dcp = tp × pcp`); 
- **Phase 2 — Backend coverage.** Like FlashAttention MLA DSA; FlashInfer GQA MLA DSA. Share PCP/DCP metadata + merge helpers across backends.
- **Phase 3 — Hybrid attention models.** Cover mixed full/sliding/DSA attention (qwen3_next, KimiLinear, etc.), parallel to the DCP `kv_cache_manager` sharding limits that already exist.

**Cross-cutting (separate PRs):
- CUDA-graph capture of the CP attention region (currently `AttentionCGSupport.NEVER` under `pcp>1`); 
- Chunked Prefill under `pcp>1`;
- P/D disaggregation (orthogonal design removes the "PCP on P nodes only" constraint); 
- multi-node CP; dynamic PCP; ring-CP, etc.

### CC List.

@LucasWilkinson @ywang96 @ZJY0516 @pisceskkk 

### Any Other Things.

## References

- **Target design:** #33403 `[WIP] pcp alternative impl` (Lucas Wilkinson).
- **Source RFC:** #25749 — original PCP RFC; agreed all-to-all-in-DCP + per-request split.
- **PCP PR:** #46330 — GQA PCP on FlashAttention (Phase 0).

title: [RFC]: Allow the DSA Indexer to Use Context Parallelism Independently
body: ### Motivation. > **RFC scope.** This RFC requests architectural feedback on allowing the DSA Indexer and Sparse MLA to use different parallel contexts. It does not propose a complete scheduling policy or optimized cross-rank communication system. The first implementation would exercise this capability only through a fixed Indexer-CP configuration while preserving the existing Sparse MLA execution path and today's default behavior. DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) has two sequential stages: 1. The Indexer scans the history-wide index cache and selects global Top-K token positions. 2. Sparse MLA reads only those positions from the latent KV cache. vLLM currently derives both stages' parallel rank, group, and world size from the same Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) configuration. Enabling DCP for the Indexer therefore also enables it for Sparse MLA. The two stages do not benefit equally from this coupling. The Indexer scans a compact cache over the full history, so its work grows with history length and can be divided across ranks. Sparse MLA reads a fixed Top-K from a much larger latent KV cache, so using more ranks adds partial-output/LSE merging and consumes ranks that could otherwise serve independent requests. Our preliminary operator benchmarks on 2x NVIDIA H20 report CP2 latency speedup as `T(DCP=1) / T(DCP=2)`. Each panel fixes batch size and query length; the x-axis is history length. The Indexer obtains substantially higher CP2 speedup than Sparse MLA across most long-context `Q>1` shapes, while both stages regress at `Q=1` because communication and launch overheads dominate. *Figure 1. CP2 latency speedup on 2x NVIDIA H20. Teal is the Indexer; red is Sparse MLA using the same BF16 KV precision across TP1 and CP2. A value above 1.0 is a latency improvement, and 2.0 is ideal linear scaling. `Q=1` denotes decode. The anomalous Indexer regions in this figure use paired random-input TP1/CP2 reruns.* The proposed path therefore initially targets only long-context `Q>1` execution. This RFC asks vLLM to stop requiring the DSA Indexer and Sparse MLA to use the same parallel context. It intentionally proposes only one concrete new mode: > Run the Indexer with a fixed CP group, then run Sparse MLA locally on the request-owning data-parallel rank. The key observation is: > DSA turns attention into a small dense read over the index cache followed by a large sparse read over the latent KV cache. The two reads should not be required to use the same parallel group. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Remove the shared-group assumption `SparseAttnIndexer` and sparse MLA backends should receive separate internal parallel contexts. The exact type should align with the ongoing [Per-Layer Parallelism Policy RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42659), but the sparse-attention interface must not assume that these values are equal: ```text indexer_parallel_context sparse_mla_parallel_context ``` For all existing configurations, both contexts resolve to today's DCP group. This keeps current behavior unchanged. This RFC does not propose a general per-state placement framework. It only leaves an explicit extension point so that a DSA backend can select a different group for its Indexer. #### 2. Implement one fixed Indexer-CP mode The first opt-in implementation uses a fixed single-node topology: - Attention is deployed with data-parallel request ownership. - Each request has one owner rank. - The owner stores the request's full latent KV cache. - The request's compact Indexer cache is sharded across a fixed Indexer CP group. - The owner sends the Indexer query to that group. - Each helper computes local Top-K candidates. - The candidates are merged and the global Top-K indices are returned to the owner. - The owner executes Sparse MLA locally without Sparse MLA CP. ```text request owner fixed Indexer CP group | | |--------- query + metadata ---------->| | | local index scans |<----------- global Top-K ------------| | | local Sparse MLA over owner-local latent KV ``` Only query metadata, new Indexer keys, and Top-K candidates cross ranks. The large latent KV cache is not migrated or repartitioned at the stage boundary. The implementation may initially use existing NCCL/PyTorch communication. It must use groups created during initialization, preserve global token indices, and handle empty helper work. An optimized transport is not required by this RFC. #### 3. Limit initial routing and fallback The new path is selected only when all of the following are true: - The model uses the supported DSA Indexer and sparse MLA backend. - Execution is single-node with a supported fixed group. - Query length is greater than one. - The request's latent KV cache fits on its owner rank. Otherwise, vLLM uses the existing local or coupled-DCP path. Unsupported configurations must fail clearly after the new mode is explicitly selected; they must not silently use an inconsistent cache layout. #### Non-goals The first RFC and implementation do not include: - Dynamic CP degree selection. - Per-request rank resizing. - A goodput-aware scheduler. - Latent-KV migration or dynamic request-owner migration. - Multi-node execution. - A new generic collective or DeepEP-like communication backend. - Changes to the existing coupled-DCP implementation. - A claim that Sparse MLA should never use CP. These may be considered separately after the fixed path demonstrates an end-to-end benefit. ### Feedback Period. Two weeks after the RFC is posted. ### CC List. ### Any Other Things. #### Correctness and evaluation Correctness tests should compare the new path with DCP=1 and existing coupled DCP for: - Global Top-K indices and model outputs. - Causal boundaries and Top-K ties. - Uneven query counts and empty helper work. - Indexer-cache append and global token-index mapping. - Repeated execution without stale communication buffers. Performance evaluation should use the same hardware, precision, kernels, memory limit, and request workload for: 1. DPA with local Indexer and local Sparse MLA. 2. Existing coupled DCP. 3. Fixed Indexer CP with owner-local Sparse MLA. The operator breakdown should report Indexer scan, query dispatch, Top-K merge, and Sparse MLA latency. The end-to-end evaluation should report TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and goodput under explicit latency SLOs. The single-GPU baseline must use the best available Indexer backend. In particular, the proposed [SM90 fused DSA prefill Indexer backend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53563) could reduce the available benefit from Indexer CP and should be included when available. #### Relationship to existing RFCs - [Per-Layer Parallelism Policy #42659](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42659) is the preferred home for resolving parallel contexts. This RFC adds the narrower requirement that two stages inside DSA may consume different contexts. - [Shared Context Parallelism #50127](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50127) may later optimize Indexer query, key, and Top-K exchange. This RFC does not depend on that optimized path. - [Dynamic Context Parallelism #29295](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/29295) addresses dynamic collaboration across DP ranks. This RFC uses only a fixed group and does not resize it per request. - [Data Parallel Attention and Expert Parallel MoEs #16037](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/16037) provides the request-owned attention mode in which owner-local Sparse MLA runs. #### Open questions 1. Should the two contexts be represented directly by #42659's parallel plan, or by a small nested sparse-attention plan? 2. Can the existing DP/EP execution order safely support a fixed cross-DP Indexer operation, including empty ranks, or is an explicit synchronization point required? 3. Should the first implementation reuse an existing DCP collective path or a Shared-CP object when both are available? #### Requested feedback 1. Is removing the shared parallel-context assumption from DSA an acceptable extension to vLLM's attention interface? 2. Is a fixed, single-node Indexer-CP/Sparse-MLA-local implementation an appropriate first scope? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Sharded Context Parallelism for Deepseek DSA
body: ### Motivation. Context Parallelism (CP) is a promising approach for scaling inference of long-context and sparse-attention models. Recent work (e.g., [arXiv:2411.01783](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01783)) highlights its key advantages: latency reduction via sequence-level compute parallelization, lower inter-node communication than Tensor Parallelism (TP), and distributed KV cache storage that scales with more devices. However, current CP implementations (e.g., RFC #22693) adopt a CP+TP hybrid design, which imposes critical limitations: 1. **Redundant weight storage across CP ranks** Although the sequence is partitioned across CP ranks, each rank still holds a full copy (or TP-sharded copy) of all weights. This prevents CP from scaling to many devices—especially at fine granularity (e.g., one rank per GPU)—as total memory usage grows linearly with the number of CP ranks. 2. **Redundant computation within CP rank** Despite sequence partitioning, each CP rank still performs standard Tensor Parallelism (TP) internally. Even when combined with Sequence Parallelism (SP), this setup leads to redundant computation within each rank. This issue is especially pronounced in sparse attention models. For example, in DeepSeek DSA, the Indexer module—which dynamically selects active tokens—cannot be parallelized via TP. As a result, every CP rank must independently execute the full Indexer logic on its local sequence, processing many inactive or irrelevant tokens and incurring substantial redundant computation that scales with the number of CP ranks. 3. **Incomplete KV cache deduplication** While PCP/DCP deduplicate KV cache across CP ranks, the cache is still fully replicated across TP devices within each CP rank, leading to redundant storage We propose **Sharded Context Parallelism**, which enables CP at the granularity of a single GPU. By i introduced the **shard linear** feature, which reduces redundant memory usage for weights, and throughout the entire process, each card only calculates a portion of the seqlen, completely eliminating redundant calculations. Looking ahead, we also plan to integrate with PCP(RFC #25749) to enable per-card KV cache sharding, extending deduplication down to the single-device level. We have implemented the initial version of the function in the vllm-ascend framework on the Ascend 910c NPU, and achieved a performance gain of 336% on deepseek-v3.2. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/4702 ### Proposed Change. We will first implement a version for deepseek v3.2 and later extend it to more models. ## sharded Context parallellism for Deepseek V3.2 The flowchart for the sharded CP for deepseek v3.2 is as follows: ## shard linear As shown in the above architecture, I used shard linear for o_proj and q_proj, because these two weights take up most of the mla. The shard linearFeature is inspired by FSDP, allowing us to store weights in a conventional TP manner. When required, the weights are asynchronously all-gathered to perform the full matrix multiplication. why broadcast? For certain hardware, it may have a private weight storage format, such as the Ascend NPU NZ format, and the FSDP's all-gather method will be invalid due to this. We have introduced the broadcast method to address the private format. This Feature has been merge into the main branch of vllm-ascend. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/2931 ## Performance comparison Compared to the CP&SP scheme of the community, our scheme takes the granularity of a single card as the CP domain, eliminating the reduce-scatter at the end of the O matrix and the all-gather of the q_lora matrix, but introduces two communications of shard linear, which we believe can be completely masked. title: [RFC]: Support Dynamic Context Parallelism
body: ### Motivation. The DP-attention + EP (Expert Parallelism) hybrid has become the de-facto standard for scaling MoE models.Nevertheless, production traffic frequently breaks the uniform-workload assumption across DP-attention shards: 1. Existing context-parallel strategies restrict tensor slicing to the intra-DP domain, so workload imbalance across DP-attention replicas remains unresolved. 2. When prefill and decode are colocated (PD colocation), the single-DP prefill phase serializes the attention computation and stalls all other DP workers, leaving GPUs idle and lowering overall utilization. 3. Under PD disaggregation, a surge of long prompts in the decode cluster abruptly inflates the KV-cache working set, prolonging the attention computation on the affected shard and creating a straggler that skews the load balance across DP-attention replicas. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/326dc749-dedc-4cd9-ac5d-376785446a73) ### Proposed Change. Our work primarily aims to realize request-level heterogeneous parallelism: for long-sequence requests, both the prefill and decode phases are handled cooperatively by multiple DP attention replicas (CP > 1), thereby mitigating GPU execution bubbles. An additional abstraction layer, termed "Domain", is introduced between the Scheduler and the DP instances, wherein each Domain governs multiple DP workers to enable dynamic allocation of computational resources on a per-request basis. To circumvent the overhead associated with the dynamic instantiation of communication parallelism groups, multiple communication parallelism groups are pre-established, and the optimal CP size is selected in accordance with the request sequence length; short-sequence requests are routed through the standard DP attention pathway (CP = 1). Furthermore, we intend to implement a request instance migration mechanism, whereby long-tail requests are migrated from CP = 1 DP instances to CP > 1 instances, so as to alleviate the queuing latency experienced by other short-sequence DP workers. The proposed modifications are confined to the Executor, EngineCore, Scheduler, KV Cache Manager, and the Attention backend; the remainder of the system remains unaltered and naturally accommodates dynamic CP configurations. 1.Within the Scheduler component, a novel `CrossDPScheduler` class is introduced, which overrides the base scheduling function to dynamically partition and allocate the requisite DP ranks in accordance with the sequence length of each individual request. The overridden function produces a `list[SchedulerOutput]` as its output, thereby accommodating the heterogeneous scheduling decisions distributed across multiple DP domains. 2.Within the Executor and EngineCore components, a `Domain` class is respectively overridden, aggregating multiple DP replicas into a unified Domain entity, thereby enabling coordinated scheduling and resource orchestration across the constituent DP workers within each Domain. 3.Within the ModelRunner component, leveraging the `scheduler_output_list`, a reordering mechanism is implemented to relocate Context Parallelism (CP) requests to the foremost positions within the batch, thereby facilitating more convenient aggregation and processing of attention scores and LSE vectors. To ensure the seamless applicability of CUDA Graph during the decode phase, a two-dimensional CUDA Graph capture strategy is currently adopted; further optimization of this approach is deferred to subsequent research efforts. 4.Within the KV Cache Manager component, a novel `CrossDPKVCacheManager` class is introduced, which employs a list-based organizational paradigm to facilitate the unified management and coordinated scheduling of Block Pools, thereby enabling efficient allocation and orchestration of KV cache resources across heterogeneous DP domains. 5.In the attention module, the implementations of CP for prefill and decode differ in several aspects. + we adopt the following strategy to implement Prefill CP(RFC https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/25749) + At decode time, attention is computed for a single token, so an all-reduce over the attention scores and LSE vectors from all DP ranks suffices. ### Co-Authors @hochen1 @lidenghui1110 @zzhx1 @jianzs @wangxiaochao6 @weiguihua2 @zhenwenqi2024 @luokui183 @HiC4Sh1e @99mycql @Levi-JQ ### Road Map #### MVP Release + Establishment and validation of the Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation pipeline. + Implementation of two discrete Context Parallelism (CP) granularity tiers. + Integration of NPU graph execution mode. + MLA adaptation targeting Kimi K2.5. + Decode Tensor Parallelism configured at degree 1 (TP = 1). #### Intermediate Release + Realized through the KV Connector component, support for runtime adjustment of CP configurations, targeting the enablement of 1M context length capability. + Support for multi-tier CP granularity, accompanied by further refinement of scheduling modeling and optimization of scheduling strategies. #### Final Release + Demonstrated performance gains across all mixed long- and short-sequence workload scenarios. + Comprehensive support for MLA, GQA, and sparse attention mechanisms (with prefill prioritization; decode support may be deemed unnecessary), each yielding measurable performance improvements. + Realized through HBM KV Pool, support for runtime adjustment of CP configurations . + Support for KV Cache redundancy elimination within the TP domain. + Dynamic instantiation of communication domains at runtime. + Within Domain Dynamic DP Load Balancing (DPLB) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Long-context-optimized Pipeline Parallelism, CPP + Async P2P + Dynamic Chunking
body:
### Your current environment

### Motivation

vLLM's current Pipeline Parallelism implementation is positioned in the [official docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/serving/parallelism_scaling/) as a *capacity or memory* fallback:

> *"Multi-node multi-GPU using tensor parallel and pipeline parallel inference: if the model is too large for a single node, combine tensor parallelism with pipeline parallelism."*

This positioning is correct for the original PP use case, but it leaves a sizable performance opportunity on the table for **long-context disaggregated serving**, where PP on the prefill side is the right tool to (a) compress the prefill pool (fewer prefill GPUs feeding the same number of decode GPUs) and (b) hide long-context attention bubbles via micro-batched stages.

[SGLang's chunked-pipeline blog (2026-01-15)](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-01-15-chunked-pipeline/) demonstrates that long-context PP needs a specific *combination* of three techniques to actually win. Reference numbers (DeepSeek-V3.1 on H20):

- **PP4 TP8 with DCK 12K → 3.31× prefill throughput** over the TP8 baseline.
- At matched GPU count (32 GPUs), **PP4 TP8 outperforms PP1 TP32 by 30.5%** with DCK, and still by 18.4% even with fixed 12K chunks — i.e. the architectural advantage is not just from dynamic chunking.
- **Strong-scaling efficiency at PP4: 82.8%** — the bubble overhead is effectively absorbed once `M ≫ P`.

vLLM today has **none** of the three pieces SGLang relies on. As a result, in our own measurements on GB300 NVL72 (DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4, ISL=128K / OSL=1, aggregated), PP4 + chunked prefill (1,536 TPS/GPU) is *slower* than PP4 with no chunking (1,678 TPS/GPU), because the existing chunked-prefill path was designed for TP-only continuous batching ([SARATHI](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.16369), [DeepSpeed-FastGen Dynamic SplitFuse](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.08671)) and does not address PP bubble reduction.


### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Proposed feature

Add a long-context-optimized PP path with the following three components, gated behind an opt-in flag (e.g. `--pipeline-parallel-mode long-context`):

1. **Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP)** — split a *single* long prompt into pipeline micro-batches that flow concurrently through stages. This is distinct from vLLM's existing chunked prefill (which targets *inter-request* decode piggybacking).
2. **Asynchronous P2P** — overlap GPU computation with stage-to-stage p2p transfers to reduce idle bubbles (today's PP path serializes compute with P2P).
3. **Dynamic Chunking (DCK)** — choose chunk size as a function of the per-request prefix length so attention runtime is roughly uniform across stages, minimizing bubbles caused by quadratic attention.

### Companion / pre-requisite

- [#40674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40674) — PP + `NixlConnector` for disaggregated serving. Long-context PP is most useful on the prefill side of disagg deployments, which today cannot use PP because of the connector gap. This RFC assumes #40674 lands first or in parallel.

### Use case / context

- Model: DeepSeek-R1 (FP4) on Blackwell (GB300 NVL72), ISL=128K / OSL=8K, disaggregated.
- Goal: shrink the prefill pool via PP on prefill workers (matching the deployment pattern already validated by SGLang on the same model class) while keeping decode on TP / DP+EP. Prefill-pool compression is the largest single architectural-level gap we observe between vLLM and SGLang on GB300 long-context.

title: [Bug]: ExampleHiddenStatesConnector full gather causes long-context OOM
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Sanitized reproduction environment</summary>

```text
Affected code: current vLLM main, ExampleHiddenStatesConnector
Hardware reproduction: vLLM 0.21.1.dev33+g7fd0329cd
Python: 3.11
Device: Ascend NPU, 61.27 GiB per device
Parallelism: TP8 x DP2
Hidden-state dtype: BF16
Extracted shape per token: 4 layers x hidden width 7168
max_model_len: 65536
max_num_batched_tokens: 8192
gpu_memory_utilization: 0.95
```

The production environment is isolated, so this is a sanitized summary rather
than the full `collect_env.py` output.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The current `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector._submit_async_write()` implementation
gathers all requested hidden states into one device tensor before allocating
pinned host memory and starting the D2H copy:

```python
hidden_states_gpu = extract_from_kv_cache(
    self._kv_cache, slot_mapping_gpu, num_tokens
)
pinned_hs = torch.empty_like(hidden_states_gpu, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
pinned_hs.copy_(hidden_states_gpu, non_blocking=True)
```

The indexed gather materializes a tensor with shape approximately
`[num_tokens, num_extracted_layers, hidden_size]` on the device. Its temporary
memory usage therefore grows linearly with the complete request length, rather
than being bounded by the scheduler's prefill chunk size.

For four BF16 hidden-state layers with hidden width 7168, the gather alone
requires:

```text
49,152 tokens: 49,152 * 4 * 7,168 * 2 bytes = 2.625 GiB
65,536 tokens: 65,536 * 4 * 7,168 * 2 bytes = 3.500 GiB
```

Consequently, a request that otherwise fits in the configured KV cache can
still fail during hidden-state export because the connector needs several
additional GiB of contiguous temporary device memory. Chunked prefill does not
bound this export allocation: the final export still gathers all `num_tokens`
at once.

### Observed failure

In a production hidden-state generation service, a 49,152-token export
attempted the exact calculated allocation and killed the engine:

```text
torch.OutOfMemoryError: NPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.63 GiB
ExampleHiddenStatesConnector
  -> extract_from_kv_cache
  -> kv_cache.flatten(0, 1)[slot_mapping]

vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError:
EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

The scheduler dump showed:

```text
num_computed_tokens=[40960]
num_scheduled_tokens=8192
slot_mapping shape=[49152]
```

The OOM propagated as `EngineDeadError`, returned HTTP 500 for the request, and
terminated the hidden-state service. A controlled reproduction with the same
full-gather implementation also failed when it attempted a 1.75 GiB gather
for 32,768 tokens while only 1.59 GiB was free.

### Expected behavior

Exporting hidden states for a valid long-context request should not require a
single temporary device allocation proportional to the complete sequence
length. The connector should be able to export the requested hidden states
without killing the engine when the model execution and KV cache already fit
within the configured device-memory budget.

### Motivation.

### Motivation

Long-context prefill is often dominated by attention computation. As context lengths grow to 64K, 128K, and beyond, dense prefill attention becomes a major deployment bottleneck even when decoding is already optimized.

We have been experimenting with a training-free sparse prefill attention mechanism called **BFLA (Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention)** for vLLM-style paged-attention workloads. BFLA is designed as an opt-in runtime attention backend: it does not modify model weights, does not require training or calibration, and falls back to dense attention for unsupported cases.

Reference implementation:

https://github.com/Alicewithrabbit/BFLA

I would like to ask whether the vLLM maintainers would be open to upstreaming this as an experimental V1 Triton attention feature, possibly in several small PRs.

### Proposed Change.

### Proposal

Add an experimental sparse prefill path to the V1 Triton attention backend.

At a high level, the method works in two stages:

1. **Runtime block-level importance estimation**

   During prefill, BFLA partitions the query and KV sequences into coarse blocks. It builds lightweight pooled Q/K representations and estimates causal block importance at runtime. The resulting block-level mask identifies which KV regions should be retained for each query block and KV head.

2. **Tile-level sparse prefill execution**

   The coarse block mask is expanded to the Triton attention tile grid. The fused prefill kernel skips dropped KV tiles while preserving exact token-level causal attention inside every retained tile. The sparse path is only used for safe prefill-like workloads; otherwise it falls back to the existing dense Triton attention path.

The feature would be disabled by default and enabled only through an explicit experimental flag or environment variable.

title: [Roadmap]Prefill Context Parallel Refactor
body:
**This refactor design is generated by Codex under supervision. Technical details are prone to changes, but the overall design will not change.**

## Motivation

The current context parallelism (CP) implementation has grown around model- and
backend-specific branches. This makes the behavior hard to reason about and hard
to extend.

Main issues:

- Server args are confusing. Generic CP, DSA CP, and deprecated NSA aliases use
  separate flags and mode fields, even though they describe the same two CP
  sharding strategies.
- CP sharding logic is coupled with model code and attention backend code.
  Zigzag (`in-seq-split`) and interleave (`round-robin-split`) are model-agnostic
  layouts, but today each model family wires them differently.
- Model coverage is asymmetric. DSA models support both zigzag and interleave;
  MLA and GQA models historically mostly supported zigzag; DeepSeek V4 uses
  interleave. The draft CP-v2 path now also validates Qwen3 interleave, which
  is a useful GQA/MoE example for the new abstraction.
- Legacy communication code is scattered. `communicator_dsa_cp.py`, CP branches
  in model files, DSA indexer logic, and attention backend logic all own pieces
  of the same layout transition.
- Some topology choices are hardcoded in server args, such as forcing
  `enable_dp_attention=True` / `dp_size=1` for interleave-style paths.

The goal is to make CP a strategy-owned runtime abstraction: server args select
whether CP is enabled and which strategy to use; models and attention backends
call strategy interfaces instead of open-coding CP-specific branches.

## Design

### 1. How Server Args Usage Changes

Before, CP had overlapping flags:

```text
--enable-prefill-context-parallel
--prefill-cp-mode {in-seq-split}
--enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel
--dsa-prefill-cp-mode {in-seq-split,round-robin-split}
--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel
--nsa-prefill-cp-mode
--attn-cp-size N
```

After, CP has one enable flag and one strategy axis:

```text
--enable-prefill-cp
--cp-strategy {zigzag,interleave}
--attn-cp-size N
```

Deprecated mode values map to the new strategy names:

| Deprecated value | New strategy |
|---|---|
| `in-seq-split` | `zigzag` |
| `round-robin-split` | `interleave` |

Deprecated boolean flags are still accepted and mirrored into
`enable_prefill_cp`:

```text
--enable-prefill-context-parallel
--enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel
--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel
```

The normalized server args initialize a process-wide CP strategy singleton.
The runtime execution path remains gated by `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` during the
transition.

### 2. CP Strategy Design

#27313 lands the strategy abstraction scaffolding and process-wide strategy
initialization. CP strategy classes own the common policy surface for a CP layout:

- whether CP can apply for a forward batch;
- how per-forward CP metadata is built;
- how hidden states and position IDs are sharded;
- how rank-local hidden states and KV payloads are gathered;
- how per-request sharding will be expressed by strategies that need it;
- how model inputs are split before `model.forward`;
- how attention dispatch, KV materialization, and attention metadata reindexing
  will be routed once the model/backend migrations land.

The module layout is:

```text
python/sglang/srt/layers/cp/
  __init__.py      # package exports, including singleton helpers from base.py
  base.py          # enums, base metadata, ContextParallelStrategy ABC, singleton helpers
  zigzag.py        # implemented former in-seq-split strategy and zigzag metadata
  interleave.py    # former round-robin-split strategy shell and interleave metadata
  utils.py         # public import facade for strategy classes and metadata
```

There is no separate `strategy.py` in this PR. The process-wide helpers live in
`base.py`; `utils.py` is only the public import facade for strategy classes and
metadata types.

Class definitions:

```python
class ContextParallelStrategy(ABC):
    name: str
    kind: ContextParallelStrategyKind
    cp_size: int
    cp_rank: int
    per_layer_attn_cp_comm: bool

    def can_apply(self, num_tokens, forward_batch) -> bool: ...
    def build_metadata(self, num_tokens, seqs_len, extend_seqs_len=None): ...
    def shard_hidden_states(self, x, forward_batch): ...
    def shard_position_ids(self, positions, forward_batch): ...
    def gather_hidden_states(self, x, forward_batch, stream=None): ...
    def gather_kv_cache(self, x, forward_batch, stream=None): ...
    def shard_per_request(self, extend_seqs_cpu, extend_seqs): ...
    def split_before_forward(self, forward_batch, input_ids, positions, input_embeds=None): ...
    def run_attention(self, q, forward_batch, device, attn_fn, attention_backend): ...
    def materialize_full_kv(self, forward_batch, layer, k, v): ...
    def reindex_attn_metadata(self, core_attn_metadata): ...

class ZigzagCPStrategy(ContextParallelStrategy): ...
class InterleaveCPStrategy(ContextParallelStrategy): ...
```

Process-wide helpers added by #27313:

```python
def init_cp_strategy(server_args) -> None: ...
def get_cp_strategy(): ...
def get_cp_strategy_kind() -> ContextParallelStrategyKind: ...
def is_cp_enabled() -> bool: ...
def is_zigzag() -> bool: ...
def is_interleave() -> bool: ...
```

`ServerArgs._handle_context_parallelism()` now calls `init_cp_strategy(self)`
after legacy CP arguments are normalized and validated. If `enable_prefill_cp` is
false, or `attn_cp_size <= 1`, the singleton is cleared. Otherwise,
`cp_strategy={zigzag,interleave}` binds either `ZigzagCPStrategy` or
`InterleaveCPStrategy`.

`get_cp_strategy()` also lazily initializes from global server args. This lets
worker processes recover the singleton after deserialization, where
`ServerArgs.__post_init__` is not rerun. The singleton and compatibility
predicates are intentionally visible under both CP-v1 and CP-v2. The
`SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` env var is introduced as a default-off runtime rollout
flag for future CP-v2 dispatch, but #27313 does not make `get_cp_strategy()`
return `None` when that env var is false.

Metadata definitions:

- `BaseContextParallelMetadata` stores `total_seq_lens` and `bs`.
- `ZigzagContextParallelMetadata` extends it with the former in-seq-split
  permutation fields, per-rank token counts, per-sequence FlashAttention tensors,
  and CPU-side diagnostic lists. `ContextParallelMetadata` remains an alias to
  the zigzag metadata shape.
- `InterleaveContextParallelMetadata` extends the base metadata and currently has
  no extra per-forward payload.

Class relationship:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ContextParallelStrategyKind {
        <<enumeration>>
        NONE
        ZIGZAG
        INTERLEAVE
        from_string()
        cli_value()
    }

    class CPAttentionBackendKind {
        <<enumeration>>
        FLASH_ATTENTION
        from_string()
    }

    class BaseContextParallelMetadata {
        total_seq_lens: int
        bs: int
    }

    class ZigzagContextParallelMetadata {
        split_list
        zigzag_index
        cp_reverse_index
        reverse_split_len
        per_rank_actual_token
        max_rank_len
        kv_len_prev_tensor
        kv_len_next_tensor
        actual_seq_q_prev_tensor
        actual_seq_q_next_tensor
        cu_seqlens_q_prev_tensor
        cu_seqlens_q_next_tensor
        total_q_prev_tokens
        total_q_next_tokens
        max_seqlen_q_prev
        max_seqlen_q_next
        kv_len_prev_list
        kv_len_next_list
        actual_seq_q_prev_list
        actual_seq_q_next_list
    }

    class InterleaveContextParallelMetadata {
        no extra payload yet
    }

    class ContextParallelStrategy {
        <<abstract>>
        name: str
        kind: ContextParallelStrategyKind
        cp_size: int
        cp_rank: int
        per_layer_attn_cp_comm: bool
        can_apply()
        build_metadata()
        shard_hidden_states()
        shard_position_ids()
        gather_hidden_states()
        gather_kv_cache()
        shard_per_request()
        split_before_forward()
        run_attention()
        materialize_full_kv()
        reindex_attn_metadata()
    }

    class ZigzagCPStrategy {
        kind = ZIGZAG
    }

    class InterleaveCPStrategy {
        kind = INTERLEAVE
    }

    BaseContextParallelMetadata <|-- ZigzagContextParallelMetadata
    BaseContextParallelMetadata <|-- InterleaveContextParallelMetadata
    ContextParallelStrategy <|-- ZigzagCPStrategy
    ContextParallelStrategy <|-- InterleaveCPStrategy
    ContextParallelStrategy --> ContextParallelStrategyKind
    ContextParallelStrategy --> CPAttentionBackendKind
    ZigzagCPStrategy --> ZigzagContextParallelMetadata
    InterleaveCPStrategy --> InterleaveContextParallelMetadata
```

Initialization flow added by #27313:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["ServerArgs._handle_legacy_cp_arguments()"] --> B["ServerArgs._handle_context_parallelism()"]
    B --> C["validate canonical CP config"]
    C --> D["init_cp_strategy(self)"]
    D --> E["base._STRATEGY"]
    E --> F["get_cp_strategy()"]
    E --> G["get_cp_strategy_kind() / is_cp_enabled() / is_zigzag() / is_interleave()"]
    F --> H["future CP-v2 model, attention, and communicator dispatch"]
```

The two strategies differ only in layout policy at this stage:

- `ZigzagCPStrategy` represents the former `in-seq-split` layout. It splits each
  sequence into `2 * cp_size` blocks and gives each rank one early block and one
  late block. This balances causal attention cost. Its shell currently builds
  base zigzag metadata and leaves concrete sharding, gather, attention dispatch,
  and KV materialization to follow-up PRs.
- `InterleaveCPStrategy` represents the former `round-robin-split` layout. It
  assigns token `i` to rank `i % cp_size`. Its shell currently builds base
  interleave metadata and leaves concrete sharding, gather, attention dispatch,
  and KV materialization to follow-up PRs.

### 3. Model Runner CP-v2 Boundary

#28421 keeps CP-v2 sequence sharding and final gather at the runner boundary
instead of embedding that orchestration in Qwen model files. The original merge
wired this path in `model_runner.py`; after the later runner refactor, the eager
extend implementation lives in
`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py`, while
`model_runner.py` remains the top-level dispatcher and avoids prefill CUDA graph
replay when a CP strategy is configured.

For an active CP-v2 extend batch, the eager runner now:

1. calls `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)` after forward metadata initialization;
2. calls `prepare_cp_forward(forward_batch)` to build
   `forward_batch.attn_cp_metadata`;
3. materializes complete input embeddings when `input_embeds` is absent;
4. calls `cp_split_before_forward(...)` to produce rank-local hidden states and
   position IDs;
5. runs `model_runner.model.model(...)` directly with sharded embeddings and
   positions, bypassing the model wrapper's legacy CP/logits path;
6. on the final PP rank, calls `cp_gather_after_forward(...)` before invoking
   the logits processor.

This makes the model boundary responsible for only two layout transitions:

- full input embeddings/positions -> rank-local CP layout before the model body;
- rank-local hidden states -> full token order before logits.

The attention backend owns the per-layer CP-v2 attention transitions. In
FlashAttention, when `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)` is true:

- KV cache writes call `cp_strategy.materialize_full_kv(...)`;
- attention calls route through `cp_strategy.run_attention(...)`.

### 4. How To Handle Communication

Communication should be owned by the layer that naturally owns the layout
transition:

- Interconnect communication between CP and EP/DP/TP, such as gather/scatter
  around MLP, is handled by `communicator.py`.
- AllGather before attention kernels is handled by CP strategies through
  `gather_kv_cache` / `materialize_full_kv`.
- Scatter/gather at model entry and exit is handled by CP strategies through
  `split_before_forward` and gather helpers.
- `communicator_dsa_cp.py` should be removed. Communication operations should
  not be exposed directly in modeling files such as `dsa_indexer.py` or
  `deepseek_v4.py`.

The base communicator owns CP `SCATTERED`/`FULL` hidden-state transitions:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    L["LayerCommunicator.__init__"] --> C["CommunicateContext.init_new()"]
    C --> Gate["_is_attn_cp_layer_comm_enabled()"]
    Gate -->|false| Normal["normal communicator dispatch tables"]
    Gate -->|true| CPTable["CP dispatch table"]

    CPTable --> A["prepare_attn: SCATTERED -> SCATTERED"]
    CPTable --> B["prepare_mlp: SCATTERED -> FULL or SCATTERED"]
    CPTable --> D["postprocess_layer: FULL or SCATTERED -> SCATTERED"]

    B --> Gather["_cp_gather_hidden_states_and_residual"]
    D --> Scatter["_cp_scatter_hidden_states"]
    Gather --> AG["attn_cp_all_gather_into_tensor"]
    Scatter --> RS["attn_cp_reduce_scatter_tensor"]
```

Exact layout dispatch should run before same-group-size shortcuts, because under
CP two tensors can have the same process group size while still representing
different token layouts.

### 5. Backward Compatibility Design

The refactor should merge gradually and stay off by default until the new path
has enough coverage.

CP-v2 runtime dispatch is controlled by `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`. 

`enable_cp_v2()` reads `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` through
`sglang.srt.environ.envs`. `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)` is the runtime
dispatch predicate for per-batch CP-v2 execution; it additionally requires
context-parallel extend mode, an initialized strategy, `input_ids`, and
`strategy.can_apply(...)`.

When `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=0`, server args still normalize the CP configuration
and initialize the strategy singleton for compatibility predicates. Runtime
dispatch should use `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)`, not `get_cp_strategy()`
alone. When `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1`, `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)` exposes
active batches to model runner, attention backends, model bodies, and
communication code. 

Compatibility details:

- Deprecated CLI flags are still parsed and warn.
- Deprecated mode flags also enable `enable_prefill_cp`.
- `ContextParallelMetadata` remains importable as an alias to the zigzag
  metadata shape.
- `cp/utils.py` exposes CP-v2 helper names such as `enable_cp_v2`,
  `is_cp_v2_active`, `prepare_cp_forward`, `cp_split_before_forward`, and
  `cp_gather_after_forward`.
- Non-DSA deprecated predicates preserve their old server-args semantics.
- DSA deprecated predicates remain in `attention/dsa/utils.py` while the CP-v2
  runtime helpers live in `cp/utils.py`.

## Roadmap
An example PR for this refactor effort can be found at #25957. It will be split into a series of smaller PRs as the following plan:
- [x] Simplify the server args usage with the new ones #27312 
- [x] Add CP strategy abstractions. 
    - [x] defined classes, metadata, add related unit tests, and add the flag `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` for backward compatibility. #27313
    - [x] Implement member functions of zigzag strategy #28421
    - [x] Implement member functions of interleave strategy #30482
- [ ] Move communication ownership into the common communicator. #28775
  - Fold DSA CP `SCATTERED`/`FULL` transitions into `communicator.py`.
  - Remove `communicator_dsa_cp.py`.
  - Keep model files focused on model computation rather than layout
        communication.
- [x] Implement the new CP design on covered model families
  - [x] Support GQA models, starting with Qwen3, also include GPT-OSS/Mimo V2.5 #29972 
  - [x] Support MLA models, including Kimi K2.5 and DeepSeek V3 #31619 
  - [x] Support DSA models, including GLM-5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 #30482
  - [x] Support DeepSeek V4 with the new CP implementation #33532
- [ ] Enhance the Context Parallel tests with long context pressure tests.
- [x] Flip `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`  to True and deprecate old CP implementation
  - [x] Deprecate CP V1 tests https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36222
  - [x]  Remove server args/environ settings related to CP V1 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36223/
  - [x]  Remove old logics in CP V1 logics https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36228 #38293 
  - [ ] Canonicalize prefill CP API names #36229 
  - [x] Update documentation for prefill CP V2 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36230
- [ ] Future enhancement, such as supporting more attention backends with CP, or adding documents

title: HiSparse Roadmap for Long-Context Sparse Serving
body:
## Motivation

HiSparse[[Blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-04-10-sglang-hisparse)] is designed to support long-context sparse attention in SGLang with much lower GPU memory usage during decode. Instead of keeping the full KV history in HBM, HiSparse keeps only a small hot working set on device and backs the full token history in CPU pinned memory, swapping selected tokens back to GPU on demand.

For 1MB-class contexts and PD serving, the main challenges are IO overhead, kernel efficiency, KV transfer cost, and compatibility with HiCache/offloading, MTP, and more sparse model families. The roadmap focuses on improving model coverage, reducing long-context overhead, and making HiSparse decode robust in production PD scenarios.

Slack Channel：kv-cache-store

## Roadmap

### 1. Sparse Model Support

- [ ] MiniMax-M3 (Call For Contribution)
- [x] DeepSeek-V4
- [x] GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.1

### 2. Performance Optimization for 1MB Long Context

- [ ] For GLM-5.2, implement IO prefetch and compute overlap based on the IndexShared mechanism to reduce IO impact. #28523 
- [ ] Make HiSparse compatible with MTP. @huangtingwei9988 
  - Option A: Dynamic balancing: use MTP for small batches and HiSparse for large batches.
  - Option B: Direct compatibility based on [sglang#26445](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26445).
- [ ] Optimize HiSparse kernels by reducing the performance impact of heavy shared-memory usage and adopting a more aggressive parallelization strategy.   @DarkSharpness 
- [ ] Support TwoBatch Overlap to hide io latency  @SYChen123 @BJWang-ant 

### 3. HiSparse Decode Optimization in PD Serving

- [ ] Integrate with the Decode L2 RadixTree stack and make it compatible with HiCache offloading. @hzh0425 
- [ ] Fix HiSparse host-backed max request length: [sglang#28753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28753).
- [ ] Prevent startup OOMs caused by over-estimating `max_total_num_tokens`: [sglang#28752](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28752).
- [x] Support NIXL DRAM KV destinations for HiSparse: [sglang#27563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27563).
- [ ] Share CPU memory across TP ranks: [sglang#27370](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27370).
- [ ] Fix HiSparse max token configuration: [sglang#25288](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25288).
- [ ] Fix DSV4 HiSparse PD state page sizes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28879
- [ ] HiSparse V2: Unified logical kv space for hisparse https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32314

### 4. Support More Training-Free Sparse Algorithms

- [ ] Add extension points for Quest and other training-free sparse attention algorithms. @magicYang1573 @Ronnie-Rui

title: MambaRadixCache shape mismatch in PD chunked prefill when caching unfinished req
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and did not find the same failure mode.
- [x] This is a correctness/stability bug, not a question.

### Environment

- SGLang version: `v0.5.12.post1`
- SGLang commit: `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584`
- Deployment mode: prefill/decode disaggregation
- Tensor parallel size per engine: `4`
- Workload: long-context rollout with chunked prefill enabled by the scheduler
- Model family: Qwen3.6 27B / hybrid attention with Mamba state cache

### What happened

A prefill scheduler process crashed while caching an unfinished chunked prefill request into `MambaRadixCache`.

The failing path is:

```text
scheduler.event_loop_normal_disagg_prefill()
  -> get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run()
  -> process_prefill_chunk()
  -> maybe_cache_unfinished_req(self.chunked_req, self.tree_cache, chunked=True)
  -> tree_cache.cache_unfinished_req(req, **kwargs)
  -> mamba_radix_cache.py:659
       mamba_value_forked = self.req_to_token_pool.mamba_pool.fork_from(mamba_value)
  -> memory_pool.py:405 fork_from()
  -> memory_pool.py:393 copy_from()
       self.mamba_cache.conv[i][:, dst_index] = self.mamba_cache.conv[i][:, src_index]
```

The exception is:

```text
RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [48, 1, 251, 1, 2560, 3]
cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [48, 1, 2560, 3]
```

This happened on all TP ranks of the same prefill engine. After that the prefill instance exited, and decode side requests cascaded into `KVTransferError`, `Connection refused`, and router `500 Internal Server Error` responses.

### Why this looks wrong

`MambaPool.fork_from()` allocates exactly one destination Mamba cache slot:

```python
dst_index = self.alloc(1)
self.copy_from(src_index, dst_index)
```

So the source index passed to `fork_from()` should identify one final Mamba state slot. In the failing chunked-prefill path, `mamba_value` appears to carry extra batch/chunk/time dimensions instead. PyTorch advanced indexing then expands the source tensor to:

```text
[48, 1, 251, 1, 2560, 3]
```

while the destination expects one cache slot:

```text
[48, 1, 2560, 3]
```

This suggests that `cache_unfinished_req(..., chunked=True)` can pass a non-scalar/non-single-slot Mamba value into the radix-cache fork path.

### Expected behavior

Caching unfinished chunked prefill requests should not crash the scheduler. For correctness, if the code cannot prove that the Mamba value is exactly one final state slot, it should not insert that Mamba state into radix cache. A cache miss/re-prefill is preferable to corrupting the radix cache or crashing the prefill instance.

### Minimal safe workaround / patch direction

A conservative mitigation is to guard just before `fork_from()` in `MambaRadixCache.cache_unfinished_req()`:

```python
if mamba_value is None or mamba_value.numel() != 1:
    logger.warning(
        "Skip Mamba radix cache for req=%s in cache_unfinished_req: "
        "expected one final Mamba state slot, got shape=%s, numel=%s",
        getattr(req, "rid", None),
        tuple(mamba_value.shape) if mamba_value is not None else None,
        mamba_value.numel() if mamba_value is not None else None,
    )
    return _skip_cache_unfinished_req(req)

mamba_value_forked = self.req_to_token_pool.mamba_pool.fork_from(mamba_value)
```

This keeps the normal single-slot path unchanged and only skips the problematic Mamba radix-cache insert. It turns the failure into a cache miss instead of a scheduler crash.

A more complete fix may need to identify why chunked prefill sometimes produces a multi-element `mamba_value` here, and either select the correct final state slot or avoid attempting Mamba radix insertion for that request.

### Related issues

- #24221 discusses Mamba radix cache correctness around chunked prefill / overlap scheduling and snapshot timing.
- #22326 tracks Mamba state checkpointing / state cache design work.
